steps.text: Line two rimmed baking sheets with parchment paper. Stir oats, coconut, peanut butter, and vanilla together in a large bowl with a spatula until well combined.

Combine sugar, milk, butter, and cocoa powder in a saucepan over medium heat. Stir occasionally and gradually bring mixture to a boil. Once boiling, stir constantly and boil for no longer than 90 to 120 seconds; if it boils for too long the cookies will turn out crumbly. Remove from the heat and pour over the oat mixture; stir until well combined.
Drop large scoops of batter onto the prepared baking sheets. Spray the back of a spoon with cooking spray, and use it to flatten the scoops, respraying as needed. Let cool to room temperature.

raw_recipe.headline: No Bakes
raw_recipe.description: No-bake recipes are great projects for kids and beginner bakers. These tasty cookies made with oats, peanut butter, and chocolate are easy and delicious.

review.reviewBody: Just like I remembered them! Easier than I remembered also. Thanks!!! A hint: before you spoon onto wax paper, let mixture cool for just a moment so it's easier to control size of cookie.

I've read all the no bake cookie recipes on this site and most of them are identical to the one I've had for almost 40 yrs. The only difference is the time you should boil the butter, sugar, cocoa and milk. I bring the cocoa mixture to a soft rolling boiling on medium high heat then I turn the heat down to medium and stir constantly for 2 minutes. A nice twist is to add almond extract instead of vanilla. For a glossy finish to the cookie only use real butter. These are my husbands favorite cookies than I've made them probably a thousand times and they have always turned out. I also use 5 T cocoa instead of the 3 or 4 the other recipes listed.

I have made these for years, this works Much Better; after removing the pot from the heat you add the peanut butter ( I prefer crunchy ) and stir until it melts and blends in, then add the vanilla (I like the mexican vanilla with the rooster on the bottle - Much Richer flavor! ) and stir it in as well. Now, with all of the liquid parts together, the oatmeal mixes in Much better. Set out on waxed paper and try to keep the kids away...

I’ve been making these since I was a kid! 
If you melt the milk, butter and sugar and bring to a boil, then stir in the peanut butter, it works better. Also, add the cocoa to the dry oats and mix, then pour the hot mixture over it. Sometimes we would skip the cocoa and just have peanut butter no-bakes!

This is the second time I’ve used this recipe. The first time i used half monk fruit and half white sugar and it turned out great. This time I cut the white sugar to 3/4 cup and 1-1/4 cup monk fruit. I also increased the amount of peanut butter to 3/4 cup. You would never know that it’s not all white sugar. Reduced the recipe by almost 1000 cal!

I'm giving this recipe three stars because I had to adjust the amount of peanut butter. 1/2 cup simply wasn't enough, and I don't think it would have been possible to mix 3 cups of oats with that little peanut butter. I doubled the peanut butter to one cup, and I used creamy peanut butter because I don't like crunchy. Also, make sure to measure the ingredients as accurately as possible. I made them once with just a tiny bit too much milk, and the cookies were extremely soft and fell apart too easily (basically, you couldn't hold one like a normal cookie and expect it not to break in half under its own weight). That being said, only adjusting the peanut butter, these were the best no bakes I've had in a long time. They remind me of the ones I used to make in school. Just be sure to bring the chocolate mixture to a rolling boil all the way through before timing it for two minutes. I have made this recipe about five times now. The cookies have taken anywhere from 45 minutes to an hour and a half to set depending on composition and ingredients. I also recommend using pancake or maple syrup as a substitute for vanilla because it gives these cookies a distinct difference in flavor that I believe has more body instead of just being "sweet chocolate-peanut butter cookie." It makes them taste more interesting and have a slight toastiness to them. Either way, these are excellent cookies if made right! I can't stop eating them.

P.S. DO NOT use almond milk. It will ruin them!

Loved them! Much easier to mix if you put vanilla and peanut butter in before the oats. I add a half to one cup of coconut with the oats-great filler and adds more texture. Both my husband and daughter hate coconut except in these cookies!! I use an ice cream scoop to put them on wax paper.

This is the same recipe my family and I have used forever. I've made these a bazillion times and have a few tips for newbies that make perfect cookies every time: 
1. measure the oats, peanut butter, and vanilla into bowls before you start so you don't have to rush and risk the mixture cooling too much
2. melt the peanut butter in the microwave before so it doesn't cool your mixture too much before you can spoon it out. 
3. stir the entire time it is boiling and try to get all the sugar off the sides of the pot while it is boiling.
4. start the 90 second timer after it comes to a FULL boil, this ensures the cookies will set.

The first time I tried this recipe, they tasted good, but they were dry and crumbly, which is weird because usually they turn into goopy messes. 

I've figured out the secret: you really do have to warm the sugar mixture SLOWLY. And 90 seconds of boiling is plenty. 

Then give them a quick moment to cool, then spoon them quickly before they cool into a crumbly state. These are so freakin good and easy it's crazy!

These are delicious. I use my large cookie scoop (1/4 cup) and it makes 13 big cookies. I also just melt all the ingredients together in a pot and add the oats at the end. Remove from heat and wait 10 mins before scooping into parchment. Tastes the same and fewer dishes ;)

These are hands down the best thing I’ve made during quarantine. This is my absolute favorite cookie and I’ve never attempted them as i’m not much of a baker. This recipe makes them just like I remember. And all the tips from the other reviewers helped so much! I only used 1.5 cups of sugar because that’s all I had left and I added an extra table spoon of cocao powder as well as an extra table spoon of peanut butter and these are so amazing! Followed the directions from another reviewer to stir the peanut butter and vanilla into the saucepan after you remove it from heat and then add the oats. Worked like a charm. Also let the mixture sit for about 5-10 mins before I balled it up on the cookie sheet. These are fantastic! And easy! Make yours today!
Well, I made up this batch to give to my son-in-law to see how he likes him
Absolutely amazing! Really easy recipe to follow, definitely recommend. FIVE STARS
Used a Tblsp of instant coffee during boil. Really amps the chocolate!
I lost my recipe for these cookies, and it was an old recipe, so I tried this one, and it's great!! Thanks for sharing!
Tasty
I am currently in a baking phase with ADHD. This was a challenge and it will be fun to make. Fast and easy. New hyper fixation!! :) easy to follow recipe and easy if you’re not good at focusing
I left everything the way it was. My children, all 10 of them, loved it.

This has been a family favorite for 55 plus years. When I married. My hubby's family made a BLOND VERSION no cocoa. Not my cup of tea but the chocolate is my go to for any time we want cookies. I gave some to the FIRE HOUSE one time and the captain said he was keeping them to himself not sharing. Don't know if he did but that was a very memorable experience
Me and my little sister made this recipe for her name day (it was st. Cecilia's feast day, and that's her name) and our mom is pregnant, so we froze the leftovers to have when the baby comes.
